subject: Post-call recap: AcmeHealth private VPC / on-prem discovery & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Reyes <john.reyes@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 14:00:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: AcmeHealth private VPC / on-prem discovery & next steps

Hi John — thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so we’re aligned. Please correct me if I mis-state anything.

Pain points & drivers
- Regulatory: HIPAA + state-level PHI rules; data must remain US-resident; some datasets are subject to tighter controls.
- Network restrictions: procurement requires strict egress policies; only allow connections to whitelisted endpoints; outbound proxies and explicit port allowances in place.
- Risk tolerance: prefer minimal shared cloud egress for PHI; air-gapped or customer-managed VPC preferred.

Goals
- Evaluate Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem options) for inference workloads (clinical note summarization & embeddings).
- Timeline: aim for Proof-of-Concept in Q3 (targeting September kickoff) if we can clear network and security gating items.

Technical constraints discussed
- Preferred deployment: Private VPC in our managed tenancy OR on-prem air-gapped cluster (depending on network feasibility).
- KMS/HSM: key management must integrate with AcmeHealth KMS or support customer-managed keys.
- Ports/endpoints: need a detailed network checklist from Redwood to validate with IT and firewall team.
- Telemetry & logs: audit logs required for SOC/HIPAA review; retention details needed.

Next steps (action owners & timing)
1) Marissa (me) will send a concise network checklist + high-level private architecture diagram — attached for first pass. (Today)
2) AcmeHealth to confirm strict network egress allowances and provide primary IT contact for technical deep dive. (This week)
3) Schedule a technical call (Redwood infra + Dev Patel) to walk the checklist and map required firewall rules. (Next week)
4) Redwood to prepare a preliminary SOW and deployment options for review. (By end of next week)

Attachments: redwood-private-architecture.pdf (high-level), redwood-sow-draft.docx (template)

If that aligns, I’ll coordinate scheduling and share the downloadable checklist link.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: John Reyes <john.reyes@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: AcmeHealth private VPC / on-prem discovery & next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. That matches our discussion. A couple clarifications / additions:

- Regulatory scope: correct on HIPAA; also need to consider state-level PHI retention rules (CA + NY for our footprint).
- Data residency: must be US-only; any replica outside US is a non-starter.
- Preferred deployment: we prefer either a Private VPC in a dedicated tenant that we control, or fully on-prem air-gapped deployment. Our security team will evaluate tradeoffs.

Looping in our IT ops lead: Sandy Lopez (sandy.lopez@acmehealth.com) — Sandy, can you confirm the team’s availability for a technical deep-dive and whether there are existing constraints (proxy, TLS inspection, non-standard ports) we should flag?

Timeline: still targeting a Sep POC but will depend on how fast IT can validate the checklist.

Thanks — John
John Reyes
Head of Applied AI | AcmeHealth
john.reyes@acmehealth.com | +1 (617) 555-0189
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Reyes <john.reyes@acmehealth.com>, Sandy Lopez <sandy.lopez@acmehealth.com>

Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: AcmeHealth private VPC / on-prem discovery & next steps

Thanks John — thanks for the intro to Sandy. Sandy — welcome, brief note on what I’m sharing and proposed immediate next steps: 

What I’ve attached/linked:
- redwood-private-architecture.pdf: high-level diagrams for Private VPC and on-prem footprint (what gets deployed, control plane flows, KMS options).
- acme-network-checklist.xlsx: preliminary checklist for firewall rules, allowed endpoints, proxy config, certificate pinning guidance.
- redwood-sow-draft.docx: template SOW to help accelerate procurement conversations (pricing TBD).

Immediate asks for IT review (can be handed to infra/network folks):
- Confirm whether outbound connections to a small set of Redwood endpoints are allowed (we can provide a FQDN/IP list).
- Confirm whether TLS inspection or proxy will break mTLS/KMS flows; if so, we’ll document alternative approaches.
- Confirm whether customer-managed VPC peering or direct connect options are required.

Proposed next steps / meeting cadence:
- Technical deep-dive (60 min) with Redwood infra + your network/security engineers — proposed windows next Tue/Wed (28/29 Jul). Dev Patel (cc) will lead the runbook walk-through.
- After technical validation, Redwood will produce a deployment proposal + preliminary SOW.

Links: Shared checklist & diagram: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cAcmeHealth-Redwood
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME/2147

If this is all good I’ll have Dev reach out to schedule the deep-dive.

Best — Marissa

On Thu, Jul 22, 2026 at 11:30 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks John — thanks for the intro to Sandy. Sandy — welcome, brief note on what I’m sharing and proposed immediate next steps: 
> 
> What I’ve attached/linked:
> - redwood-private-architecture.pdf: high-level diagrams for Private VPC and on-prem footprint (what gets deployed, control plane flows, KMS options).
> - acme-network-checklist.xlsx: preliminary checklist for firewall rules, allowed endpoints, proxy config, certificate pinning guidance.
> - redwood-sow-draft.docx: template SOW to help accelerate procurement conversations (pricing TBD).

Thanks Marissa — I reviewed the checklist and attached an initial firewall/export rule set that reflects our current posture (attached: acme-network-checklist.xlsx with comments). A few notes from my side: 
- We have TLS inspection on our corporate proxy. For an on-prem air-gapped deployment, TLS inspection does not apply, but for any managed VPC deployment we will need to understand mTLS and certificate pinning implications.
- We cannot allow any outbound connections to third-party regions (non-US). All endpoints must be US-only.
- Ports: we generally allow 443 outbound, and a limited set of additional ports via a change window — will need a list of exact ports and IP ranges.

I’m available for a technical deep-dive Tue Jul 28 at 10:00am ET or Wed Jul 29 at 2:00pm ET. Please confirm and include Dev Patel to walk the runbook.

Regards — Sandy
Sandy Lopez
IT Operations Lead | AcmeHealth
sandy.lopez@acmehealth.com | +1 (212) 555-0147
